_comment: failure_mode -> deterministic remedy, as DATA not code (the requirements.json idiom). Keys in failure_mode MUST match the choice values in scripts/jev_annotate.py QUESTIONS.failure_mode exactly; tests/test_jev_remediate.py fails the build if the two ever drift. ORDER IS SIGNIFICANT: entries sharing a failure_mode form a ladder, cheapest rung first, and the driver picks the first entry whose grounding check passes. loopable=false means do NOT retrace -- report and stop; the reason/next_step fields are the operator-facing explanation. Every remedy is a table lookup on a choice value plus bounded arithmetic: no model output ever becomes a parameter value.
_grounding_note: grounds_in lists preflight/validate_svg RULE ids (the finding 'rule' field). An entry is grounded when ANY cited rule is present in the candidate's findings -- not all -- because the modes pair a Layer A rule with a Layer B one (COLOR_COUNT is declared-property, COLOR_COUNT_RENDERED is rendered). CRITICAL: the check deliberately ignores severity. preflight.py:241-244 (the _ALWAYS_ADVISORY frozenset, members on 242-243) marks NODE_COUNT and PALETTE as advisory ('production quality, not printability'; 'a stray colour may be deliberate'), so a check filtered to hard findings would refuse both of the two loopable modes forever as not_grounded.
_metrics_note: metrics name the deterministic numbers that define progress for the mode, in priority order; ANY improves with NONE regressing counts as an improvement. This replaces the plan doc's 'count of hard findings for the grounded rule (want 0)' as the sole primary metric: that number is structurally 0 both before and after for geometry_overload and palette_mismatch, because both rules are advisory by design, so it can never detect progress and would let a no-op iteration report success. 'rule_findings' below counts findings for the grounded rule at ALL severities. Metrics are read from the manifest's stats/stats.static, never from Jev's score.
_metrics_source_note: off_palette_colors is NOT lifted into the projected state by jev_annotate._compact_stats (which lifts the string palette_conformance instead), so a palette_mismatch iteration must read the manifest rather than the sidecar for its metric. Flagged, not fixed, in this pass.
_deviations_from_plan_doc: geometry_overload gains a tracer-free primary rung (node_reduce). docs/remediation-loop.md:471 states 'There is no node simplifier in the repo' and §4/§7 conclude geometry_overload is the one mode that always needs a retrace. scripts/node_reduce.py now exists in chopshop-svg and is a deterministic, targeted, transactional post-processor with --dry-run/--json and an explicit rejected_regression outcome, so the premise is obsolete. (The plan doc now carries a header note pointing here, so the paragraph itself is left as the historical record.)

screen_explosion/snap carries needs_tracer=false, matching §4's own classification of 'screen_explosion colour stage' as tracer-free (~0.1s). The plan's §2 table lists needs_tracer=true on that same snap entry; the two sections contradict each other and §4 is the correct one, since snap_colors.py is a pure post-process on an existing SVG.

needs_tracer means 'requires the vtracer backend to be re-run', NOT 'requires chopshop-svg'. Every remedy here shells out to chopshop-svg tools; the flag drives cost ordering and the prefer_tracer_free policy.

remedies._why: Cheapest rung: node_reduce.py post-processes the SVG that already exists, touching only paths over the gate. It escalates its own deviation tolerance internally (doubling to tolerance_cap) so the loop does not step it, and it self-reports via --json (status, gate_cleared, path_nodes_max_before/after). Exit 3 / status rejected_regression means the fit would have worsened a path: that rung failed, escalate to the retrace rung below -- it is NOT an error.

Escalation only, for when node_reduce cannot fit the artwork within tolerance. filter_speckle drops small shapes at the tracer, which removes whole paths rather than smoothing them -- a different mechanism, so it can succeed where simplification fails.
Second escalation: a higher layer_difference merges gradient layers, cutting node count at the source. poster's built-in value is 16 (trace_sweep.py PRESETS), so the ladder starts there.

remedy.note: cheapest: no retrace. Prefer this before dropping color_precision.

remedies._why: Measured: snap_colors.py --force took a 677-colour trace to 4 colours, so the tracer-free rung reaches the budget far more often than intuition suggests. snap_colors.py exit 1 (colours remain off palette) means this rung failed -- escalate, do not treat it as an error.

remedy.floor_note: color_precision=2 collapses to 1 colour (measured) -- the range floor is 4, not 0.

remedies._why: Only reached if the snap cannot reach the budget. The floor is enforced by the range check, not by clamping: the plan doc is explicit that a loop free to walk color_precision down without a floor will destroy the artwork.

Tighten the snap tolerance so near-misses stop being left unmatched. snap_colors.py --tolerance default is 32.0. Rungs 1-3 of the colour ladder preserve geometry byte-identically, so a colour remedy can never worsen geometry_overload and the two modes cannot interfere.

remedies.reason: Tone cannot be reproduced by flat spot inks at any trace setting. This is a print-route decision (process halftone / DTG), not a trace-parameter one. Looping burns candidates for no outcome.
remedies.next_step: surface print_route from the same verdict to the operator

remedies.reason: A missing or failing tool (inkscape/gs/qpdf/poppler) is an environment fault. Retracing cannot fix it and will fail identically.
remedies.next_step: fail the iteration loudly and report the missing tool

remedies.reason: Nothing to remediate. Stop -- a retrace has no target and any change is a random walk.
remedies.next_step: hand the run back to the human pick

remedies.reason: The measurements did not identify one signature, so no remedy can be justified.
remedies.next_step: ask for a human review, or improve measurement fidelity first
